arms.title: BD-062: the clock read answers a caller without administrator rights, the set still does not
arms.note: Every other call of this suite arrives over ssh and is elevated, so no existing arm can see this defect: it would read the clock as an administrator. The probe runs bc250kmd_cli clock read in the console session, as the user who is logged on there, at the limited run level, through a scheduled task that it removes again. mhz, vid and temperature_mc must all be in that answer. Then the same read from the elevated session must still give a live reading, and clock set 1000 820 from the non-elevated task must be refused. It ends on the health of the part: no GPU fault line and the fan still at state=curve controlling=1. It changes no setting and no clock, and the operating point it names in the refused set is the one the lab already runs at.

arms.title: BD-080: a logon that is not an administrator confirms the driver start
arms.note: The suite cannot reach this defect either: every installer arm logs on as the lab's administrator account, which the defect never affected. The arm makes a local account that is not in Administrators, arms the automatic logon for two starts, restarts, and then reads what the two logons left: a confirmation line and the window task's line in start-confirm.log, the window task's last result 0, UnconfirmedStarts back at 0, the clock control still on, both scheduled tasks registered, and no Microsoft Basic Display Adapter. The password is generated on the lab and never printed. Windows keeps it in plain text in the registry while the automatic logon is armed, which is why the cleanup step removes the value, the account and its profile, and why the cleanup runs as a post step on every exit path. The boot waits are target.py boot --after-now, as the rule of 2026-10-11 requires. Why it is an operator arm and not a trial: it restarts the machine twice and waits for two logons, so no three-minute bound can hold it.

arms.title: BD-126: the firewall notification window on the processor route, and back on the adapter
arms.note: The repro needs no game: a program that listens on a network port from a path with no firewall rule makes Windows raise the 'Windows Security' window, and svchost.exe starts PickerHost.exe to draw it. The listener is a copy of powershell.exe under a name of its own, started in the console session through a scheduled task, because no window of this kind appears in session 0. The default phase wants route=cpu with reason=app-dialog-host, the allow phase wants route=gpu with reason=app-default, and the restore phase puts the AppRouter values back from its own record. The two shots are the only evidence that the window paints its text and its two buttons, which no script can read: they are optional steps, so a missing shot fails nothing, and the operator looks at them. If the window stays empty on the processor route as well, the entry buys nothing and comes out (driver/umd/router/README.md). The application GPU UMD's own log of that process needs a machine-wide DXVK_LOG_PATH, because svchost.exe starts the dialog host.

failure_classes.symptom: Quake II RTX hangs the GPU about 27 s in: the process stops presenting, the KMD reports a fence timeout or a ResetEngine, and the run ends on its bound with no frame rate.
A Vulkan client freezes before its first present: the route and the swap chain are created, no present row is ever written, and the process stays alive with no fault and no TDR.
A long compute packet ends in bugcheck 0x116 with parameter 3 0xC0000001: our own private submission budget trips on healthy work and the recovery after it fails.
A planned restart is read back as unclean: the arm after a restart reports an unexpected shutdown although the restart was this suite's own.
A WinUI window of the control application comes up blank: the window exists and its content never renders.
The lab's sshd accepts nothing for minutes: the call itself returns no output, or fails at the banner exchange, while the machine is otherwise alive.
